title: Lovable raises $400M Series C at $13.3B, doubling its December valuation
subtitle: The Stockholm vibe-coding startup is on a $600M revenue run rate less than two years after launch, with Menlo Ventures leading and EQT Scaleup Europe co-leading the round.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Stockholm-based Lovable closed a $400 million Series C at a $13.3 billion post-money valuation on August 12, 2026, roughly double the $6.6 billion mark it hit last December. Menlo Ventures led, with EQT's Scaleup Europe Fund co-leading. The named participant list runs long — Balderton Capital, Carmignac, Kaszek Ventures, LTS Growth, Tencent, World Innovation Lab, Regent, Accel, Antler, CapitalG, DST Global, Evantic Capital, HubSpot Ventures, and Salesforce Ventures — a spread that reads as an index fund on the vibe-coding category rather than a conviction bet on one company.

The revenue numbers are what the round is priced on. Founded in 2023 by Anton Osika and publicly launched in November 2024, Lovable now reports users have created more than 60 million projects on the platform, and Lovable-built applications receive over 900 million visits per month. The company is on track for an annualized revenue run rate approaching $600 million by the end of August 2026 — close to triple the level disclosed in December 2025. That is one of the fastest revenue ramps in software history, and it is what carries the $13.3B tag.

This lands in a category — natural-language-to-app tools, now widely called 'vibe coding' — that has become one of the most crowded and best-funded in the AI stack. Cursor, Replit, Anthropic's Claude Code, GitHub Copilot Workspace, and Bolt/StackBlitz are all fighting for the same developer and prosumer audience, and each has raised or repriced significantly in the last twelve months. What separates Lovable in the pitch decks is European reach and a template-first onboarding path aimed at non-developers rather than professional engineers.

A note for learners: a valuation-to-revenue multiple of roughly 22× (13.3B on a projected 600M run rate) is high even by AI-era standards, and it only pencils out if usage keeps compounding at the current rate. If you're joining or evaluating a company in this space, ask not 'how big is the round?' but 'how retained is the monthly cohort?' — vibe-coding platforms live and die on whether users come back next month to iterate, or churn out after building one weekend project.
